A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AlphaDecay study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching experiments moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLaMa pretraining experiments on C4, ViT training on ImageNet-1K, ablations, timing measurements, and six-seed statistical comparisons.

after.justification: V3 retains original training experiments and adds zero-shot reasoning, GLUE fine-tuning, and GPT-nano results in Section 4.3.

M1.justification: The Hill estimator, use of the largest half of the eigenvalues, linear module-wise decay assignment, and default 500-step update interval are unchanged. Algorithm 1 now writes out the existing assignment formula rather than referencing Equation 3; this does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: V3 adds seven zero-shot benchmarks: ARC-c, ARC-e, PIQA, HellaSwag, OBQA, WinoGrande, and BoolQ, plus eight GLUE fine-tuning tasks. These substantially broaden task and data coverage beyond v1's language-model pretraining and image classification. C4 and ImageNet-1K were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Uniform, AWD, and AdaDecay remain the principal comparison methods, including in the new evaluations. However, the retained ViT comparison drops the no-weight-decay control reported as 65.12% in v1 Table 5. The AdamW and statistical comparisons preserve their comparator membership after moving to the appendix.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 introduces zero-shot evaluation of pretrained LLaMa-1B checkpoints using lm-eval-harness default prompts, RoBERTa-base fine-tuning on GLUE, and a GPT-nano pretraining configuration. These are substantial additions to the evaluation design. The previously stated LLaMa training settings in Tables 1 and 6 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The assignment-function, spectral-metric, fitting-method, update-gap, and scaling-range analyses remain unchanged, including Figures 5–9. A limited reduction concerns sensitivity evidence for vision: v1 Table 5 compares ViT results at 5e-6 and 1e-6 weight decay, whereas v3 retains only scores matching the latter row.

E5.justification: The six runs with seeds 5–10, mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting, and paired t-tests are retained unchanged from v1 Table 4 to v3 Table 13. Timing uncertainty in Table 10 is also unchanged. The new benchmark tables introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V3 Tables 3–5 add substantial results: AlphaDecay versus Uniform averages are 43.35 versus 41.50 on zero-shot tasks and 85.12 versus 83.83 on GLUE; GPT-nano perplexities are 27.37 versus 27.56. Table 4 shows seven GLUE wins across eight tasks, despite prose saying six of seven. Shared larger-model C4 results and relocated AdamW/statistical results are unchanged. The full 60M Adam comparison and ViT results at zero decay and 5e-6 are omitted; the remaining ViT row matches v1's 1e-6 results.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.4 derives the Hill exponent estimator through Pareto-density normalization, likelihood construction, and maximum-likelihood estimation. V1 states the estimator without this derivation. This adds mathematical reasoning for an existing component without changing the estimator or introducing a new performance guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about spectral imbalance, HT-SR-guided module-wise weight decay, and improved performance across pretraining scales. The new evaluations provide additional support without revising those core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds interpretations that pretraining gains transfer to zero-shot reasoning and that AlphaDecay also works in RoBERTa fine-tuning and another language-model architecture. The spectral-balancing explanation and stated limitations concerning MoE evaluation and interactions with other optimization techniques remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 specifies lm-eval-harness and default prompts for the new zero-shot evaluation. It removes v1 Section 4.6's ViT-specific description of 120 epochs, Adam, and ConvNeXt training configurations, and no longer labels the retained ViT scores with their decay value. Existing LLaMa implementation details and the code link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The ConvNeXt paper, 'A ConvNet for the 2020s,' and its training-configuration citation are removed. The remaining references match after renumbering, and the related-work discussion and novelty positioning are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 locally reorganizes the empirical narrative: it adds Section 4.3, moves AdamW and paired-test sections to Appendices B.1–B.2, and makes the previous Appendix B into B.3. It also adds Appendix A.4, corrects HR-SR to HT-SR, and updates author information. Most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The main empirical displays are substantially reorganized: new downstream Tables 3–4 are added, Table 5 becomes a cross-architecture summary, Table 2 loses its 60M columns, and the former AdamW and statistical tables move to the appendix as Tables 12–13. Figures 1–9 retain their graphics, with limited caption clarifications.

improvement.justification: The new zero-shot and GLUE comparisons directly strengthen evidence for downstream usefulness beyond pretraining perplexity, while Appendix A.4 makes the estimator's derivation more self-contained. Most existing experimental support is preserved. The improvement is qualified by sparse settings for the new evaluations, removal of ViT training details and control results, and the GLUE prose/table win-count inconsistency. These support a positive but limited overall quality gain.
